subject: history
topicDisplay: World History Topic Authoritarian States 20th Century
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The Locarno Treaties, marking a high point of Stresemann's foreign policy by guaranteeing Germany's western borders, were signed in which year?
questions.explain: The Locarno Treaties of 1925 confirmed Germany's western frontiers and improved relations, paving the way for League of Nations membership.

questions.q: In which year did Germany invade the USSR in Operation Barbarossa?
questions.explain: Operation Barbarossa, the German invasion of the Soviet Union, began on 22 June 1941.

questions.q: The Great Leap Forward, Mao's drive for rapid collectivisation and industrialisation, was launched in which year?
questions.explain: The Great Leap Forward began in 1958, organising peasants into vast people's communes.

questions.q: What did the New Economic Policy (NEP) of 1921 permit?
options: Limited private trade and small business
questions.explain: The NEP allowed a tax in kind and limited private trade to revive the shattered economy.

questions.q: The compilation of Mao's quotations distributed to promote his cult was popularly known as what?
questions.explain: The 'Little Red Book' of Mao's quotations, edited by Lin Biao, became central to the cult of Mao.

questions.q: In which year did the People's Republic of China take over China's seat at the United Nations from Taiwan?
questions.explain: The PRC replaced Taiwan in the UN, including the Security Council seat, in 1971.

questions.q: The nationwide anti-Jewish pogrom known as Kristallnacht ('Night of Broken Glass') took place in which year?
questions.explain: Kristallnacht occurred on 9-10 November 1938, with synagogues burned, Jewish businesses destroyed and tens of thousands arrested.

questions.q: In which month and year did the monarchy fall in the February Revolution?
questions.explain: The February Revolution of 1917, in early March by the Western calendar, led to Nicholas II's abdication.

questions.q: Whose 1934 assassination is often seen as a pretext for the Great Terror?
questions.explain: The murder of Leningrad party boss Sergei Kirov in December 1934 was used to justify mass purges.

questions.q: In which year was Khrushchev removed from power?
questions.explain: Khrushchev was ousted by his Presidium colleagues in October 1964, ending the period studied.

questions.q: Which 1918 treaty took Russia out of World War I?
questions.explain: The Treaty of Brest-Litovsk (March 1918) ended Russian participation in WWI at great territorial cost.

questions.q: In what year did Stalin die, paving the way for new leadership?
questions.explain: Stalin died in March 1953, beginning a power struggle eventually won by Khrushchev.

questions.q: What event of 22 January 1905 triggered the 1905 Revolution?
questions.explain: On Bloody Sunday troops fired on peaceful petitioners led by Father Gapon at the Winter Palace.

questions.q: What was the harsh economic policy of the Civil War period called?
questions.explain: War Communism (1918-21) involved grain requisitioning and nationalisation to supply the Red Army.

questions.q: The 1932-33 famine hit which region especially hard?
questions.explain: Ukraine suffered catastrophic famine (the Holodomor) during 1932-33 amid collectivisation.

questions.q: Which figure was named Mao's designated successor before dying in a plane crash in 1971?
questions.explain: Lin Biao, named Mao's successor in 1969, died in a plane crash in Mongolia in 1971 after an alleged failed coup.

questions.q: Which 1936 initiative aimed to prepare the German economy and armed forces for war within four years?
questions.explain: The Four-Year Plan of 1936, overseen by Goering, prioritised rearmament and autarky to ready Germany for war by 1940.

questions.q: Who succeeded Mao as head of state and, with Deng Xiaoping, led pragmatic recovery after the Great Leap famine?
questions.explain: Liu Shaoqi became head of state in 1959 and, with Deng Xiaoping, implemented economic recovery measures.

questions.q: The Hundred Flowers Campaign, encouraging intellectuals to voice criticism, mainly took place in which year?
questions.explain: The Hundred Flowers Campaign reached its height in 1957 before being abruptly reversed.

questions.q: The 'Three-Anti' and 'Five-Anti' campaigns of the early 1950s targeted whom?
options: Corruption among officials and the urban bourgeoisie
questions.explain: The 1951-52 campaigns attacked corruption, waste and bureaucracy among officials and capitalist businessmen.

questions.q: What slogan summed up Bolshevik appeal in 1917?
questions.explain: 'Peace, Land and Bread' captured Bolshevik promises to a war-weary, hungry population.

questions.q: Which war's defeats helped spark unrest in 1905?
questions.explain: Humiliating defeats in the Russo-Japanese War of 1904-05 fuelled discontent leading to revolution.

questions.q: The Treaty of Versailles, which Germany was compelled to sign, was concluded in which year?
questions.explain: The Treaty of Versailles was signed in June 1919, imposing territorial losses, disarmament, reparations and the 'war guilt' clause on Germany.

questions.q: The 1950 Marriage Law in the PRC is significant for doing what for women?
options: Outlawing arranged marriage and granting the right to divorce
questions.explain: The 1950 Marriage Law banned arranged marriages and concubinage and gave women the right to divorce.

questions.q: In which year did Alexander II issue the Emancipation Edict freeing the serfs?
questions.explain: The Emancipation of the Serfs was decreed in February 1861, freeing roughly 23 million privately owned serfs.

questions.q: At which 1956 Congress did Khrushchev denounce Stalin's crimes?
questions.explain: Khrushchev's 'Secret Speech' attacking Stalin's cult of personality was delivered at the 20th Party Congress in 1956.

questions.q: Stalin's first Five-Year Plan, launched in 1928, prioritised what?
questions.explain: The first Five-Year Plan (1928-32) emphasised heavy industry such as coal, steel and machinery.

questions.q: The Dawes Plan, which restructured German reparations and brought in US loans, was agreed in which year?
questions.explain: The Dawes Plan of 1924 rescheduled reparations and provided American loans, helping to stabilise the German economy.

questions.q: In which year was the Federal Republic of Germany (West Germany) established with its Basic Law?
questions.explain: The Federal Republic of Germany was founded in 1949 with the adoption of the Basic Law, with Konrad Adenauer as its first Chancellor.

questions.q: In which month did the Bolsheviks seize power in 1917?
questions.explain: The Bolsheviks took power in the October Revolution of 1917 (early November by the Western calendar).
